subject: Arcadia Labs — private deployment: custody / escrow proposal and redlines
messages:
From: Jordan Miller <jordan.miller@arcadia-labs.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@arcadia-labs.com>, legal@arcadia-labs.com
Date: Thu, 01 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment — custody / escrow ask & redlines

Hi Rachel,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Were moving toward an order form + private deployment (VPC-hosted in our account) and legal has a few non-negotiables before procurement will sign. High level: Arcadia requires a custody/escrow mechanism for the event of vendor insolvency or long-term service interruption. Specifically: 

- Source or build artifact escrow with an independent escrow agent (triggered on failure to deliver SLA for 60+ days)
- Audit rights for our third-party security assessor (annual, limited scope)
- A defined evidence package (deployment scripts, operator runbook, DB export procedures) to be delivered on escrow trigger

Attached are their suggested redlines against the MSA and the Draft Addendum — please review and let me know if Redwood can accept a compromise (were flexible about a reproducible build pathway instead of raw source).

Jordan Miller
Director, Contracts & Security
Arcadia Labs
[Attachment: Arcadia-Redlines_MSA_Addendum_20270401.pdf (pdf)]
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Miller <jordan.miller@arcadia-labs.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 01 Apr 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment — custody / escrow ask & redlines

Jordan — thanks for the clear summary and for sending the redlines. Ive looped in Marissa (legal) and Neha (security) plus Karthik for commercial context. Were committed to making private deployment safe for Arcadia while protecting Redwoods IP. Initial questions for clarity: 

1) Is Arcadia asking for full source deposit (tarball + build system) or are you open to an escrow that contains reproducible build artifacts and a verified build recipe?
2) For the audit rights, do you need unfettered access or a scoped annual assessment with COC (non-disclosure) and pre-scheduled windows?
3) Timing: is this a hard procurement gating item for signature or a post-signature compliance deliverable?

Well review the suggested MSA edits and respond with an internal compromise proposal by EOD Friday.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Senior Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Miller <jordan.miller@arcadia-labs.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 10:07:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Private deployment — custody / escrow ask & redlines

Jordan / team — thanks, we reviewed Arcadias markups. Redwood wants to avoid full source escrow; however, we can offer a layered solution that we believe meets Arcadias objectives while limiting IP exposure: 

- Reproducible Artifact Escrow: deposit deterministic build artifacts and a cryptographic build manifest with an independent escrow agent. Escrow release triggers limited to catastrophic events (insolvency, sustained SLA failure > 60 days, or bankruptcy).
- Attestation + Operator Snapshot: quarterly signed attestation of operator-runbook currency, and a secure encrypted snapshot of deployed binaries + configuration that can be restored by Arcadia's on-prem team or by a certified third-party operator under strict non-disclosure and usage constraints.
- Scoped Audit Rights: annual third-party security assessment with a pre-agreed scope (no source code disclosure). Assessors sign our standard NDA and must agree to on-site policies.

I attach our proposed addendum language and a short checklist of the evidence package we can deliver on escrow release. If Arcadia insists on raw source, we will need a commercial concession (higher fees or escrow-only licensing with a negotiated license fee).

Attachments:
- Private-Deployment-Checklist.pdf
- Redwood-Private-Deployment-Addendum_v3.docx

Proposed next step: 30-minute call Tues 04/06 to run through each trigger and the escrow mechanics (agent, custody chain, encryption keys).

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Miller <jordan.miller@arcadia-labs.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@arcadia-labs.com>, legal@arcadia-labs.com
Date: Sat, 03 Apr 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Private deployment — custody / escrow ask & redlines

Marissa — appreciate the quick read. A few notes from legal/CTO after internal sync: 

- Reproducible artifact escrow is promising, but Arcadia needs stronger verifiability. Our preference is an escrow package that includes a reproducible build manifest *and* a minimal set of source files required to rebuild the runtime (not full repo history). Were open to a negotiated carve-out list.
- Operator snapshot: acceptable if the snapshot is encrypted with an escrow-controlled key thats only released under the same triggers; also want the runbook and operator checklist included in escrow.
- Audit rights: scoped and prescheduled is fine, but well need explicit SLAs around remediation windows for critical findings and a commitment to provide evidence artifacts (logs, traces) for the assessment period.

If Redwood is willing to accept a limited-source deposit (minimal subset + escrow restrictions) in exchange for a 12% uplift on annual fees for the first 12 months, we can likely get procurement to sign quickly. Otherwise, procurement will push for full-source escrow.

Jordan
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Miller <jordan.miller@arcadia-labs.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 04 Apr 2027 09:38:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Private deployment — custody / escrow ask & redlines

Jordan — thanks, that helps. Internal position summarized: 

- Redwood can accept a limited-source escrow (defined file list + reproducible manifest) with escrow release triggers as proposed.
- Commercial concession: were open to a one-time 10–15% uplift or a time-limited escrow fee (your preference). Karthik will propose exact pricing on the call.
- Audit/remediation: we can provide scoped annual assessments and a documented remediation timeline for critical/high findings; evidence artifacts will be provided under a signed COC and assessor NDA.

Karthik — can you prepare two commercial options (10% uplift vs. flat escrow fee) and capture the numbers in DocuSign-friendly language? Neha — can security prepare a short list of what we will and will not include in the limited-source package so we can share with Arcadia prior to the call?

Rachel
Senior Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Copy. Ill draft two commercial options (10% uplift option and a flat escrow admin fee option) and circulate an updated order form by EOD Monday. Will also add a one-sentence SLA credit commitment tied to escrow release (to address the procurement ask).
